title: Why You’re Always Broke (It’s Not Your Salary)
script:
Picture this: you’re sitting on a cluttered coffee table, your wallet feels heavier than a sack of lead, yet you swear you’re “earning enough” because your salary looks nice on paper. You says it, you hear it: “It’s not my salary.” That’s the story we’re about to juggle—why you’re always broke, and why the paycheck alone won’t light up the bank account. Ever notice how the same Monday, you shuffle out the door, your paycheck lands, and the money just… disappears?

“I have to catch the bus, grab lunch, budget a coffee—oh wait, I just paid Uncle Billy’s overdue loan.” It’s a pattern: the dollars you make seem to dissolve like a sugar cube in a hot kettle. Why? Let’s dig.

Your salary can look generous because it’s one figure on your statement. But hidden behind that neat number is a cascade of deductions: taxes, benefits, retirement contributions. Suddenly, that “good pay” shrinks to a fraction of what you actually get to keep.

It's like buying a house and then realizing you still need to pay the upkeep. And if you’re renting, the landlord’s rent‑increase card keeps sliding into your debt stack with every month. Then come the lifestyle choices.

Dinner out, streaming subscriptions, the urge to upgrade that shoes‑and‑watch combo. You jump from one small indulgence to the next, and before you know it, your emergency fund is a myth. It’s not that you’re overspending out of spite—it’s that every “just a drip” becomes a tide.

You might have a budget, but if it’s static, not living, you’ll hit walls. A rigid spreadsheet can feel like a prison. What if budgeting was a living, breathing thing?

A flexible system that senses your cash flow and real‑time guilt—calling you to plan during that sudden sale or surprise bonus. So, you’re not “broke because of your salary”—you’re blanketing every dollar under a cloud of traffic tickets, unexpected bills, and the relentless avalanche of instant gratification. The trick? Pull back.
